acceptance: Slice plan recorded in context before the first code commit; if the work is split, each further slice exists as its own tracker item with needs, and the needs that other items hold on this one point at the last slice (show_item on those items confirms it).

Refresh data come from dsdgen -update, generated before the maintenance timer starts; a test asserts dsdgen is not invoked between the timer start and stop, and that two runs at the same scale factor and refresh-set index produce identical per-table row counts and per-column checksums.

Loading the refresh files into staging tables happens inside the timer through the engine's native loading path (not adapter.load_data unless the guardrail's test passes); a test fails if file reading moves before the timer.

Each maintenance interval starts at the earlier of first submission or first read of the refresh data (clause 7.4.9.1) and excludes connection open, initialize() and close; a test records event order.

The 11 spec functions (seven LF_*, four DF_*) exist as set-based SQL over the clause 5.3.11 views; a statement-counting test shows each function issues a bounded number of statements independent of refresh row count, and no per-row UPDATE remains (grep -n 'UPDATE ' benchbox/core/tpcds/maintenance_operations.py shows none issued per row).
grep -n 'time.time()' benchbox/core/tpcds/maintenance*.py finds no use for a duration, and the timer hygiene tests from tpcds-maintenance-timer-hygiene-20261103 still pass.

Result metadata carries a maintenance method identifier; comparison of results with different identifiers behaves as the owner recorded in tpcds-maintenance-data-source-decision-20261103, and a test pins it.
Smoke: a DuckDB TPC-DS SF0.01 run with the maintenance phase completes with the new data source and reports each function's interval; paste the summary in the PR.

If docs/internal/tpc-measured-intervals.md exists on the base branch, update the rows this change affects; otherwise append the row text to the context of tpc-measured-intervals-reference-20261103. Changelog fragment states that maintenance timings before this version are not comparable.

2026-11-06 owner decision (Joe, answering a choice dialog about the refresh-key collision): "A: kit keys, PKs not enforced in maintenance". Background: in TPC-DS kit tools/scaling.c, getUpdateBase() reads arRowcount[nTable - S_BRAND] while setUpdateScaling() writes arRowcount[nTable]. Refresh order and ticket ids therefore start at 1 and overlap the base keys (SF0.01 catalog orders 1-8 against a base maximum of 1600). Keep the kit's keys unchanged. Maintenance must not run against enforced primary keys: refuse with a clear message, or declare the keys not enforced, per platform. DF returns deletes stay scoped by in-range sales (order or ticket number plus item). Owner action: report the kit bug to the TPC.
description:
Implement the option the owner recorded in tpcds-maintenance-data-source-decision-20261103. Do not start until that item is done and its context quotes the choice. This description assumes option A (dsdgen refresh sets); if the owner chose B or C, rewrite this item first as part of closing the decision item.

Spec (TPC-DS 4.0.0): refresh data must be generated with dsdgen and that execution is not timed (5.2.3); loading the refresh data, including into a staging area, is timed and must use generic or vendor loaders, not a TPC-DS-specific loader (5.2.5, 5.2.7); a maintenance function's interval starts at the first read of the refresh file (7.4.9.1). Re-read 5.3 for the function definitions.

Timer hygiene (connection setup and initialize() outside each interval, monotonic durations, deterministic generator) is owned by tpcds-maintenance-timer-hygiene-20261103, which lands first; this item must not regress it.

Function scope: implement the 11 spec functions (seven LF_* inserts and four DF_* deletes, clause 5.3) as set-based SQL over the views defined in clause 5.3.11, over staged refresh tables loaded from the dsdgen files. The spec has no UPDATE functions, so the per-row UPDATE handlers in maintenance_operations.py are removed; perf-tpcds-maintenance-set-based-20261031 is superseded by this item under option A and is closed as superseded when the owner records that option.

Decision gate inside this item. Before any code, append a slice plan to context: the PR slices (for example: dsdgen -update generation outside the timer; timed staged load through the adapter's generic loader; spec-defined maintenance functions; timer boundaries and clocks), what each changes, and the order. If the work needs more than one PR, create one tracker item per slice with needs between them. Then either make this item the umbrella that finishes last, or move the needs that other items hold on this one (tpcds-qphds-spec-metric-implementation) to the last slice item; the dependents must not unlock after the first slice. Do not land a partial maintenance rewrite as complete.

Guardrails for all code work: work only in a linked worktree (make worktree-create); never edit the primary clone. No explanatory comments or docstrings in source (make comment-policy-check). Durations use benchbox.utils.clock.mono_time()/elapsed_seconds(). Add a changelog.d/ fragment. Cited line numbers are orientation only: re-read the named symbols, docs and spec clauses before editing and treat a mismatch as a reason to stop and update this item. No live-cloud runs without owner approval; heavy runs only through make heavy-run or a lock-taking entry point. Green focused tests are not release certification. Maintenance results from the new method carry a method identifier so older and newer results are never compared silently.  Do not load refresh data through adapter.load_data unless a test shows it only appends to dedicated staging tables, never truncates a warehouse table, and aborts on any rejected row (Snowflake's load_data truncates and uses ON_ERROR='CONTINUE'); otherwise use the engine's native COPY or read path into staging, inside the timer. Official export of QphDS stays off until tpcds-qphds-spec-metric-implementation says otherwise.
